comment: The section defines trustworthy AI through effectiveness, safety, transparency, accountability, fairness, and oversight. It does not distinguish trustworthiness as an evidenced property from public trust as a social response.

anchor.note: p.108 l.Lines 154-168 read as the printed page; section 5.4.2 agrees

public.text: The section defines trustworthy AI through effectiveness, safety, transparency, accountability, fairness, and oversight. It does not distinguish trustworthiness as an evidenced property from public trust as a social response.
public.suggestedRevision: Clarify that trustworthiness must be demonstrated through evidence and governance, while trust should not be demanded from users or treated as a substitute for accountability.
